source.title: Webhook: request bodies with charset=ISO-8859-1 fail with 422 "Unknown encoding: iso-8859-1"

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

Webhook requests whose Content-Type declares a charset name that Node.js Buffer does not know are rejected before the workflow runs:

HTTP 422 {"code":422,"message":"Failed to parse request body","hint":"Unknown encoding: iso-8859-1"}

ISO-8859-1 is the IANA name of the charset Node calls "latin1". The same request with charset=latin1 is accepted and decoded correctly.

The webhook body parser passes the charset from the header straight to Buffer.toString():
- parseIncomingMessage sets message.encoding = parameters.charset.toLowerCase()
- packages/cli/src/middlewares/body-parser.ts -> parseBody() calls rawBody.toString(encoding) for JSON, XML, form-urlencoded and text bodies

The same problem was fixed for the HTTP Request node in #11928 / #11930 (binaryToString switched to iconv-lite), but the webhook body parser still uses Buffer.toString().

Real-world sender: SMS gateways (e.g. brevis.one) forward incoming SMS as application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=ISO-8859-1. Other legacy systems do the same.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Webhook node (POST, path "charset-test", Respond: when last node finishes) and activate it.
2. curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:5678/webhook/charset-test" -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=ISO-8859-1" --data-binary "text=Gr%FC%DFe"
3. Response: 422 Failed to parse request body - Unknown encoding: iso-8859-1
4. Same request with charset=latin1 -> 200, text = "Grüße"


### Expected behavior

The body is decoded with the declared charset ("Grüße"), as the HTTP Request node already does since #11930.

Suggested fix: in parseBody() decode with iconv-lite (already a dependency of n8n-core), e.g. iconv.decode(rawBody, encoding ?? 'utf-8'), or fall back when Buffer.isEncoding(encoding) is false.
